extraction.name: MMMU
extraction.description: A massive multi-discipline multimodal understanding and reasoning benchmark for evaluating multimodal models on college-level problems across six disciplines, 30 subjects, and 183 subfields.
extraction.creator: Xiang Yue; Yuansheng Ni; Kai Zhang; Tianyu Zheng; Ruoqi Liu; Ge Zhang; Samuel Stevens; Dongfu Jiang; Weiming Ren; Yuxuan Sun; Cong Wei; Botao Yu; Ruibin Yuan; Renliang Sun; Ming Yin; Boyuan Zheng; Zhenzhu Yang; Yibo Liu; Wenhao Huang; Huan Sun; Yu Su; Wenhu Chen
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The benchmark was created in three stages: selecting subjects based on availability of useful visual inputs, recruiting over 50 university students including co-authors to collect multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and create new questions when necessary, and applying multi-stage quality control including duplicate detection, format/typo checking, and difficulty filtering.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Multimodal questions sourced from college exams, quizzes, textbooks, online sources, and lecture materials.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Potential duplicates were identified using lexical overlap and source URL similarity, then reviewed by authors and removed; problems were standardized for format and typos; authors assigned difficulty levels and excluded about 10% of very easy problems.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data cleaning included duplicate detection, author review, format standardization, typo correction, and exclusion of very easy problems that did not meet benchmark design criteria.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Over 50 university students, including co-authors and specializing in relevant majors, served as annotators to collect multimodal questions from textbooks and online resources and create new questions when necessary. Annotators were instructed to follow copyright and license rules and to avoid questions with immediately available answers to reduce contamination.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Authors reviewed suspected duplicates, checked formatting and typos, categorized problems into four difficulty levels, and later analyzed 150 randomly sampled GPT-4V error instances with expert annotators to identify root causes. The paper also notes 2% annotation errors among analyzed model errors.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in the selected majors and subjects; 90 college senior students were also involved as human experts for evaluation, with 3 student experts per subject.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: A version change log exists in the supplementary material, and the leaderboard is live-updating.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Annotator and evaluator attributes include discipline/subject specialization and student status; human evaluation involved college senior students.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark is intended to monitor progress toward Expert AGI, which the paper links to risks of job displacement and economic disruption, and the authors believe it can help develop next-generation multimodal foundation models.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The manual curation process may carry biases.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark may contain biases from manual curation, focuses on college-level subjects, and is not sufficient by itself to test Expert AGI because there is no direct mapping to the 90th percentile of skilled adults and college exams are not the only relevant tasks.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking and evaluation of multimodal models for zero-shot, few-shot, validation, and test settings; the dataset is split into a few-shot development set, validation set for hyperparameter selection, and test set.

name.evidence: We introduce MMMU : a new benchmark designed to evaluate multimodal models on massive multi-discipline tasks demanding college-level subject knowledge and deliberate reasoning.

description.evidence: We introduce the Massive Multi-discipline Multimodal Understanding and Reasoning ( MMMU ) benchmark, a novel benchmark meticulously curated to assess the expert-level multimodal understanding capability of foundation models across a broad scope of tasks. Covering 30 subjects across 6 disciplines, including Art, Business, Health & Medicine, Science, Humanities & Social Science, and Tech & Engineering, and over 183 subfields.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: Data Quality Control. To further control the quality of our data, we perform two steps of data cleaning. In the first stage, lexical overlap and source URL similarity are employed to identify potential duplicate problems. These suspected duplicates were then reviewed by the authors to identify and eliminate any duplications. The second stage involves distributing the problems among different co-authors for format and typo checking... In the third and final stage, the authors categorize the problems into four difficulty levels: very easy, easy, medium, and hard. Approximately 10% of the problems, classified as very easy and not aligning with our design criteria due to their simplistic nature, are excluded from the benchmark.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: In the second stage, we recruit over 50 university students, including co-authors, specializing in these majors as annotators to assist in question collection. They collect multimodal questions from major textbooks and online resources, creating new questions based on their expertise where necessary. The annotators are instructed to adhere to copyright and license regulations, avoiding data from sites prohibiting copy and redistribution. Given the arising data contamination concems of foundation models, the annotators are advised to select questions without immediately available answers, such as those with answers in separate documents or at the end of textbooks.

rai:dataBiases.evidence: MMMU , like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: We shall caution that MMMU is not a sufficient test for Expert AGI, as per the definition [57], because there lacks a direct mapping between performance on MMMU and “90th percentile of skilled adults,” nor are college exams the only tasks an AGI shall tackle... MMMU , like any benchmark, has limitations despite its comprehensive nature. The manual curation process may carry biases, and the focus on college-level subjects might not be sufficient for testing Expert AGI [57].

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: MMMU , constituting 11.5K questions, is divided into a few-shot development set, a validation set, and a test set. The few-shot development set includes 5 questions per subject, and the validation set, useful for hyperparameter selection, contains approximately 900 questions, while the test set comprises 10.5K questions... Our evaluation is conducted under a zero-shot setting to assess the capability of models to generate accurate answers without fine-tuning or few-shot demonstrations on our benchmark. We also report the few-shot results of some selected models in the Appendix.
